channel.title: Inspiration Grid — Photography
channel.description: Recent photography inspiration selected by Inspiration Grid.

item.title: Interplanetary Travel: Dani Guindo Turns Iceland Into a Mars Basecamp
item.description: Photographer Dani Guindo captures Iceland as an alien world in Interplanetary Travel, a striking series commissioned by outdoor products manufacturer Heimplanet.

item.title: Nighttime Stories: Neon Portraits by Oliver Takac
item.description: Slovak photographer, colorist and cinematographer Oliver Takáč creates atmospheric images that feel like stills pulled from movies we’ve never seen.

item.title: Versailles Dressed in Red and Blue: Stunning Photography by Aishy
item.description: Paris-based photographer Aishy transforms the Château de Versailles into a vivid collision of color in this series titled Versailles Dressed in Red and Blue.

item.title: Poland and Beyond: Landscape Photography by Mikołaj Gospodarek
item.description: Polish photographer and travel writer Mikołaj Gospodarek captures landscapes shaped by dramatic light, changing seasons and a deep curiosity about place.

item.title: Vienna Symphonies: Monochromatic Architecture by Thomas de Franzoni
item.description: Italian photographer Thomas de Franzoni returns to the grid with Vienna Symphonies, a striking black-and-white study of the city’s architecture as musical notation.

item.title: The Extraordinary Framed Landscapes of Marcin Zajac
item.description: Polish landscape photographer Marcin Zajac has a remarkable ability to reveal familiar places from entirely unexpected perspectives.

item.title: Until the Water: Haunting Portraits of Louisiana’s Changing Landscapes by Frank Relle
item.description: For more than six years, Louisiana photographer Frank Relle has explored the state’s bayous, lakes and swamps after dark, creating a collection of images that feels suspended somewhere between documentary photography and a dream.

item.title: Dramatic Global Landscapes: Photos by Max Terwindt
item.description: Dutch photographer Max Terwindt captures the planet at its most dramatic, travelling from frozen polar regions and volcanic landscapes to deserts, tropical forests and flower-covered fields.

item.title: Tiny Worlds and Everyday Adventures by David Gilliver
item.description: Scottish photographer David Gilliver transforms food, household objects and familiar pop-culture references into playful miniature worlds through his ongoing Little People series.

item.title: Personal Perspectives: A Curated Show Marking 50 Years of Leica Galleries
item.description: Leica Gallery Wetzlar is marking a major milestone with Personal Perspectives, a special exhibition celebrating 50 years of Leica Galleries through 50 photographs selected from across the brand’s international gallery program.

item.title: Spacetime Light Sculptures by Elliot McGucken
item.description: American fine art photographer and physicist Dr. Elliot McGucken turns remote landscapes into stages for luminous cosmic events, suspending spiraling forms of light above deserts, rock formations, coastlines and mountain ranges.

item.title: Cinematic Car Photography by Sevian Daupi
item.description: Modena-based photographer Sevian Daupi captures cars with the eye of a filmmaker, turning automotive shoots into moody scenes filled with atmosphere, movement and style.

item.title: Where Roads Disappear: Radoslav Sviretsov’s Journey Through Iceland’s Highlands
item.description: Bulgarian landscape photographer and architect Radoslav Sviretsov, who is now based in Iceland, is back on the grid with a new photo essay that ventures far beyond the country’s familiar waterfalls, beaches and roadside viewpoints.

item.title: A’ Design Award & Competition 2026/2027 Early Entry Now Open
item.description: The early entry period for the 2026–2027 edition of the A’ Design Awards & Competition is now open, with an early submission deadline of June 30.

item.title: Somewhere in Japan: Candid Photos by Vincent Versluis
item.description: Amsterdam-based photographer and art director Vincent Versluis approaches Japan less like a traveler and more like a director, photographing the country as a series of held, spontaneous moments rather than a checklist of sights.

item.title: Snow Over the City: Cinematic Photography by Viktor Balaguer
item.description: French photographer and visual storyteller Viktor Balaguer turns Saint Petersburg into a frozen cinematic stage in Snow Over the City, a series shot across the Russian city in winter.

item.title: Color as a Disguise: Creative Portraits by Nassia Stouraiti
item.description: Athens-based freelance photographer Nassia Stouraiti creates portraits that treat the face as a surface for colour, texture and transformation.

item.title: Lepidoptera: Macro Photos of Butterflies and Moths by Eugenijus Kavaliauskas
item.description: Lithuanian photographer Eugenijus Kavaliauskas turns butterflies and moths into striking studies of colour, pattern and texture in his macro series Lepidoptera.

item.title: Stills Launches a Figma Plugin That Keeps Image Licensing Inside the Creative Workflow
item.description: Photo licensing platform Stills has launched a new Figma plugin, giving designers a more direct way to search, test and organize licensed imagery without leaving their working files.

item.title: The Shape of Memories: Riccardo Magherini’s Layered Visions of Hanoi
item.description: Italian photographer Riccardo Magherini returns with a new chapter of The Shape of Memories, an ongoing photographic body of work we first featured in 2016 through his Bangkok series.

item.title: Atmospheric Architectural Photos by Alexey Kozhenkov
item.description: Latvian photographer Alexey Kozhenkov captures architecture with a sharp eye for scale, symmetry and mood, focusing on buildings that feel both monumental and strangely detached from their surroundings.

item.title: The Year’s Most Inspiring Designs: 2026 A’ Design Award Winners
item.description: From groundbreaking architecture and visionary interiors to packaging, furniture, technology and conceptual works pushing the boundaries of creativity, the A’ Design Award & Competition continues to spotlight the projects defining the future of global design.

item.title: Luminous Macro Worlds: Insect Wings Captured by Chris Perani
item.description: Back in 2018, we featured Chris Perani’s astonishing macro photographs of butterfly wings, and his ongoing Wings series continues to push that process into even more intricate territory.

item.title: Photographer Kenta Hayashi Turns Tokyo’s River Traffic into a Luminous Composite
item.description: Japanese photographer Kenta Hayashi turns Tokyo’s waterfront into a shifting field of motion, with a series of long-exposure captures that culminate in a dense, almost…

item.title: Utopia Broadcasting: Otherworldly Industrial Landscapes by Serena Ho
item.description: Australian fine art photographer Serena Ho, now based in Iceland, transforms the country’s industrial and architectural landmarks into eerie dispatches from an imagined world.

item.title: Graphite and Silence: Fog Studies by Darrel Rhea
item.description: Seattle-based photographer Darrel Rhea is back on the grid with Winter Light, a series of monochrome images captured during foggy winter mornings at Washington State’s Skagit Bay Estuary.

item.title: Architecture in Motion: The Spatial Studies of Derek Pedrós
item.description: Madrid-based photographer and director Derek Pedrós approaches architecture as something to be activated rather than observed.

item.title: Sculpted Symmetry: The City of Arts & Sciences Captured by Ryû Janvier
item.description: French photographer Ryû Janvier takes Valencia’s City of Arts and Sciences and treats it like a lesson in symmetry, scale and surface.

item.title: Alien Landscapes: Infrared Photography by Roland Kraemer
item.description: Munich-based photographer and visual artist Roland Kraemer turns familiar terrain into something unrecognizable in Alien, an ongoing series that pushes landscape photography into stranger territory.

item.title: Magnetic Dance: Ferrofluid Photos by Jeremy Spaunhurst
item.description: Seattle-based photographer Jeremy Spaunhurst explores the intersection of fluid dynamics and image-making, capturing ferrofluid as a shifting, responsive material.
